issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Pneumatic.raisePressure(int) to return void, but in the solution repository Pneumatic.raisePressure(int) is declared to return boolean, while the implementing classes (LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster) provide void implementations. This creates a conflicting specification and a compilation/runtime mismatch: students following the UML/problem statement will implement/expect a void method, whereas the solution interface uses boolean, and the solution's implementations contradict its own interface.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the return type of raisePressure(int) across all artifacts. Either (A) change the Pneumatic interface in the solution to declare void raisePressure(int pressureIncrease) so it matches the UML/problem statement and the current implementations, or (B) update the UML/problem statement to specify a boolean return and change the implementing methods to return boolean values. Ensure the interface and all implementing classes use the same return type so the code compiles and students are not confused.
